Google first invested $900 million in SpaceX in January 2015. By September 30, Alphabet held 555 million shares in the rocket maker, with the stake accounting for approximately 95% of its reported stock portfolio with market value of $83.7B. Despite a 12% dip in SpaceX's share price during the quarter, the investment had grown nearly 93-fold in value since the initial investment.
Meanwhile, Alphabet trimmed position in Ethos Technologies
. Alphabet initiated a new position in Qualcomm

, While Google already develops its own Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), Qualcomm could play a significant role in bringing Gemini directly to Android devices powered by Snapdragon chips, creating another avenue for the companies to capitalize on growing AI adoption.
